title: optimize-evals-sync-agenda-and-1on1-prep
content:
Meeting: Optimize / Evals weekly sync (prep + 1:1 followups)
Owner: Jamie Park
Date: 2025-02-20 10:00am PT (sync) / 11:00am PT (1:1 with Ravi)
Goal: triage the recent quality regressions surfaced by the nightly eval run, agree on next steps for prompt-set updates and canary A/B rollout plan, assign owners and timelines.

Agenda (30m sync / 20m 1:1):
- Quick status (3m): highlight metrics that regressed since 2025-02-15 baseline
- Failures & clusters (8m): review top failing prompt sets and failure modes
- A/B canary results (7m): summarize canary vs baseline win-rate / perf tradeoffs
- Prompt-set decisions (7m): decide updates vs rollback vs model-variant routing
- Action items & owners (5m)

Notes / Observations (from nightly run: 2025-02-19 03:00 UTC):
- Baseline model: redwood-1.3b-fp16 (prod)
- Test model: redwood-1.3b-quant-v2 (candidate)
- Overall eval suite win-rate dropped from 92% -> 85% (delta -7pp).
- Top affected suites: customer-support-40 (win-rate 78% -> 60%), long-summarization-25 (74% -> 64%), code-snippet-gen-30 small regressions across edge-case tests.
- Hallucination/incorrect-fact flags increased notably on knowledge cutoff checks in customer-support-40 (examples attached in GH-PR-4521).
- Latency improved by ~12% p50 on candidate variant (good), but some generation truncation observed on prompts with long context windows (likely KV-cache quantization artifact).

Failure clusters (examples):
- Prompt-set: customer-support-40
  - Failure mode: incorrect policy citation or invented policy details (hallucination).
  - Notes: looks like model defaults to generic phrasing instead of quoting policy snippets we include in context.
  - Representative failing case IDs: EVAL-CUST-1123, EVAL-CUST-1147.

- Prompt-set: long-summarization-25
  - Failure mode: missing salient events in timeline summaries, repeated phrases, early truncation on >1500 token contexts.
  - Hypothesis: quantized KV cache causing weaker long-range attention fidelity.

A/B Canary summary (last 48h):
- Traffic: 10% of eval traffic routed to candidate model variant.
- Metrics: automated pairwise comparison (n=420 examples)
  - Candidate "wins" 38% of head-to-head, baseline wins 62% (weighted by severity).
  - Candidate has better latency and token cost (-14% token cost) but lower factuality score on the customer-support suite (-20% relative).

Initial hypotheses to test:
1) Quantization profile for candidate compresses KV cache leading to early truncation and hallucination on long-context prompts.
2) Tokenization differences or soft prompt drift cause policy-citation style changes.
3) Small sampling/temperature defaults mismatch between eval harness and serving causing distributional shift.

Quick experiments to run (owners + ETA):
- Run targeted KV cache fidelity tests across 50 long-context examples with higher-precision KV paths (no quant) to isolate quantization impact. Owner: Samira Cho. ETA: 2025-02-24.
- Re-run customer-support-40 with deterministic sampling (temp=0) to check if generation variance explains hallucinations. Owner: Jamie Park. ETA: 2025-02-21 (quick run).
- Ab-test prompt prefix that explicitly instructs model to "quote policy verbatim" vs current prefix. Owner: Ravi Patel. ETA: 2025-02-23.
- Compare tokenization outputs between candidate and baseline on edge-case inputs to see drift. Owner: eng-infra (Ivan). ETA: 2025-02-25.

Rollout options to discuss in meeting:
- Option A: Pause candidate rollout for hosted API; continue internal experiments. (Pros: avoids exposing regressions; Cons: delay lat/cost improvements)
- Option B: Limit candidate to Dedicated customers or non-critical routes where latency/cost matters more than rare factuality issues. (Requires routing policy change)
- Option C: Deploy prompt-level overrides (prefixed instructions) for affected routes while continuing rollout.

Decision checklist for sync: 
- Do we pause broad rollout? (Y/N)
- Which prompt-sets need immediate prefix/guardrails? (list)
- Who owns the regression RCA and on what timeline?

Action items (post-meeting synth):
- Jamie: run deterministic sampling reruns (customer-support-40) and upload diffed outputs to GH-PR-4521. Due 2025-02-21.
- Samira: run KV-fidelity experiment with higher-precision path, share results + metrics. Due 2025-02-24.
- Ravi: prepare two prompt-prefix variants and A/B config in the eval harness; coordinate with rollout-engine for a 5% prefix-only canary. Due 2025-02-23.
- Ivan (eng-infra): tokenization parity check and report. Due 2025-02-25.
- Jamie + Product: draft short customer note if we need to limit candidate on hosted API (decision dependent). Due 2025-02-26.

Notes to bring to 1:1 with Ravi (11:00am):
- Go over the customer-support failing examples and decide which are acceptable risk vs unacceptable.
- Prioritize prompt-set changes vs model changes; get Ravi signoff for a small prefix rollout.
- Check resource needs for accelerated KV experiments (GPU hours) and ask for approval if > 50h.

Open questions / things to follow up:
- Do we have a quick way to flag hallucination severity so A/B wins are weighted appropriately? (talk to metrics)
- Is there historical precedent for quantization causing this exact hallucination pattern? (ask research: recent quantization notes)
- Should we add a short eval harness that measures "policy-quote fidelity" as a new metric for customer-support-40?

Attachments / links: GH-PR-4521 (diffed failing examples), CONFLUENCE-OPT-234 (eval plan), JIRA-EVALS-98 (regression ticket).

Quick draft for meeting start (2 lines):
"We saw a -7pp regression in our nightly eval when testing redwood-1.3b-quant-v2. We need to decide whether to pause the rollout or mitigate via prompt-level guardrails while we run targeted KV and tokenization tests."

Scratchpad / notes to self: 
- If we pause, prepare a rollback playbook with exact traffic-migration steps (talk to rollout-engine).
- Consider short-term mitigation: route critical customer-support requests to baseline for next 48h, keep candidate on lower-tier non-critical routes.
- Tag possible follow-up: deep-dive with quant research (Samira + research team) for a paper-style writeup if root cause is quantization.

End of doc.
